speaker: Unknown
en: Please join me in welcoming to the stage Molly O'Shea and John Carlson.
zh: 请和我一起欢迎登台的 Molly O'Shea 和 John Carlson。

speaker: Unknown
en: John, thank you very much.
zh: John,非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Paul, thank you very much.
zh: 还有 Paul,非常感谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope you guys are all having a really great day enjoying everything browser-based.
zh: 我希望你们大家今天都过得很愉快,享受一切基于浏览器的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're going to talk about payments, agentic commerce, and everything that's going on in the computer.
zh: 所以我们要谈谈支付、智能体商务,以及这台计算机上正在发生的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Stripe processed $1.9 trillion in 2025, up 34%.
zh: 那么,Stripe 在 2025 年处理了 1.9 万亿美元,同比增长 34%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sounds right.
zh: 听起来没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you rebuilding for AI?
zh: 你们如何为 AI 进行重建?

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, it's really interesting right now because we've been working on Stripe for a long time, right?
zh: 你看,现在真的很有意思,因为我们做 Stripe 已经很长时间了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: This is our 17th year doing it.
zh: 这是我们做这件事的第 17 个年头。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for many years, the payments industry didn't really change that much.
zh: 而且很多年来,支付行业其实没有太大变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now, there's just like some small changes happening where, I mean, leave aside everything that's going on in stablecoins and like all that other interesting stuff.
zh: 现在呢,正在发生一些小小的变化,我是说,先不提稳定币领域正在发生的一切,以及其他所有那些有趣的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But other than that, it's all same old.
zh: 但除此之外,一切还是老样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So instinct is real.
zh: 所以 instinct 是真实存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Muse is real.
zh: Muse 是真实存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these things are real.
zh: 所有这些东西都是真实存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, you have people in the audience.
zh: 再说,台下就有很多人在用。

speaker: Unknown
en: You saw a significant fraction of the audience using them.
zh: 你看到相当大比例的观众正在使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And OK, I think it turns out, one, filling out a web form is not a value-add activity for anyone.
zh: 而好吧,事实证明,第一,填写网页表单对任何人来说都不是一项有增值的活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: No one chooses to fill out web forms in their spare time.
zh: 没有人会选择在空闲时间里填写网页表单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the whole conceit of these agents, and obviously, again, this is where browser base and computer use comes in, but when you have the stateful context where your agent knows things about you, like the basic one is it knows your shipping address and payment details and things like that, and then when it can manipulate a computer and go off and do things in the real world, it turns out it's much nicer to be able to say, hey, please renew my driver's license for me, or whatever the task is, rather than go play with web forms.
zh: 所以我认为这些智能体的整个构想——显然,这又是 browser base 和计算机使用发挥作用的地方——但当你拥有有状态的上下文,你的智能体了解关于你的一些事情,比如最基本的是它知道你的收货地址和支付信息之类的东西,然后当它能够操控一台计算机、去现实世界里做事情时,事实证明,能够说一句“嘿,请帮我续办驾照”,或者 whatever 那个任务是什么,比去摆弄网页表单要愉快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I actually think
zh: 所以我真的认为

speaker: Unknown
en: One big part of all these personal agents starting to work is actually giving them a meaningful amount of compute so you can go do stuff.
zh: 这些个人智能体开始奏效的一个重大因素,实际上是给它们足够多的算力,这样你就可以去做事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But another one is computer use actually becoming a mature enough technology because computer use is the ultimate backwards compatibility layer for the real world.
zh: 但另一个因素是计算机使用真正成为了一项足够成熟的技术,因为计算机使用是现实世界的终极向后兼容层。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how long would you need to wait?
zh: 比如,你需要等多久?

speaker: Unknown
en: For, you know, the DMV to add an MCP.
zh: 等你知道,DMV 添加一个 MCP。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I'm not a betting man, but I'm betting we would have to wait a few years.
zh: 我不是一个爱打赌的人,但我打赌我们得等上好几年。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it doesn't matter, because computer use solves that.
zh: 但这不要紧,因为计算机使用解决了这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so again, it's the ultimate backwards compatibility there.
zh: 所以再说一次,它是那里的终极向后兼容层。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've mentioned that agentic commerce is a complete rewiring.
zh: 那么你提到智能体商务是一次彻底的重构。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you mean by it's complete rewiring?
zh: 你说它是彻底的重构,是什么意思?

speaker: Unknown
en: A few things.
zh: 有几点。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is, like, it's rewiring things at the surface level where how businesses sell is going to change pretty significantly.
zh: 第一是,它在表层层面重构了事物,企业售卖东西的方式将会发生相当显著的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, the first order of change is that we think people's agents are going to be doing a huge amount of the commerce for them.
zh: 比如,第一阶的变化是,我们认为人们的智能体将会为他们完成大量的商务活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second change is maybe, or the second order change, is it probably changes the commerce landscape a little bit.
zh: 第二个变化,或者说第二阶的变化,是它可能会在一定程度上改变商务格局。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, again, I don't know what people bought in their experiences, but my experience of doing AI-powered product research
zh: 再说,我不知道大家在体验中买到了什么,但我做 AI 驱动的产品研究的经验是

speaker: Unknown
en: It often actually surfaces niche brands or businesses you haven't heard of.
zh: 它经常真的会浮现出你没听说过的利基品牌或企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's quite a good story for the long tail of businesses.
zh: 我认为这对长尾企业来说是一个相当好的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's quite empowering that if you have a product that actually is well-reviewed and that people like on the internet, it leads to more discovery of that.
zh: 我认为这相当赋能:如果你有一个在互联网上评价确实很好、人们喜欢的产品,它就会带来更多的曝光发现。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the existing aggregators are going to have to answer questions, because in a way, AI discovery is the new point of aggregation for commerce.
zh: 所以我认为现有的聚合平台将不得不回答一些问题,因为在某种意义上,AI 发现是商务的新聚合点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you probably have a bit of a turning over of the top businesses that's going to happen, where if you are selling a really good product, if you're making it discoverable, then you can kind of shoot up in the rankings.
zh: 所以头部企业可能会发生一定的洗牌,如果你在卖一个真正好的产品,如果你让它可被发现,那么你就可以在排名中迅速窜升。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the analogy for this is when, like...
zh: 我认为这方面的类比是,比如……

speaker: Unknown
en: Facebook and Instagram ads targeting was so good that it led to a whole new generation of companies that were built around, you know, targeting on those platforms and they were native to it.
zh: Facebook 和 Instagram 的广告定向投放是如此之好,以至于它催生了围绕在这些平台上进行定向投放而构建的全新一代公司,它们是这些平台的原生者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Think of a Wish.com or a Teespring or, you know, even Timu and Sheehan.
zh: 想想 Wish.com 或 Teespring,你知道,甚至 Timu 和 Sheehan。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, to a significant degree grew up on those platforms and did a huge amount of customer acquisition on those platforms.
zh: 而且,你知道,它们在很大程度上是在那些平台上成长起来的,并在那些平台上完成了大量的客户获取。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were able to more natively adopt it than the prior generation of big box retailers, who in theory had all the same tools available to them, but they were just less native to that kind of customer acquisition technology.
zh: 而且它们能够比上一代大型连锁零售商更原生化地采用这种方式,后者理论上拥有完全相同的工具,只是它们对那种客户获取技术不那么原生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, it's got to flow all the way downstream to the product creation and things like that.
zh: 而且,你知道,这会一路向下传导到产品创造之类的事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like AI e-commerce will be somewhat similar where first order, it will make buying things more convenient.
zh: 我觉得 AI 电商会在某种程度上类似,第一阶,它会让买东西更方便。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second order, it will probably actually reshape the product and the merchant landscape to favor the people who can most successfully adopt it.
zh: 第二阶,它可能实际上会重塑产品和商家格局,偏向那些能够最成功地采用它的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, how are you thinking about cybersecurity risk as that scales?
zh: 那么,随着这种规模扩大,你们是如何思考网络安全风险的?

speaker: Unknown
en: We have invented a new technology that is available to defenders and available to attackers.
zh: 我们发明了一种新技术，防御者可以用，攻击者也可以用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people make all the trite analogies to the emergence of the motor car.
zh: 而人们会拿汽车的诞生来做那些老生常谈的类比。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bank robbers were the first to adopt the car to conduct bank robberies.
zh: 银行劫匪是最早采用汽车来实施银行抢劫的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And pretty quickly, police forces started realizing, hmm, we really need cars to keep up with these bank robbers.
zh: 很快，警察部门开始意识到，嗯，我们真的需要汽车才能追上这些银行劫匪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you always have this like cat and mouse offense defense game that's happening.
zh: 所以你总是会看到这种猫捉老鼠式的攻防博弈在进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in our case,
zh: 在我们的情况里，

speaker: Unknown
en: The new models have really advanced cyber capabilities.
zh: 新模型确实具备了非常先进的网络攻击能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's, I mean, somewhat intimidating because you're realizing that the standard for, I mean, the good news is that Stripe has been very paranoid on cyber for many, many years.
zh: 这有点让人不安，因为你意识到标准是……我的意思是，好消息是 Stripe 在网络安全方面已经很多年、很多年都保持高度警惕了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's not like this is kind of totally new news for us.
zh: 所以这对我们来说并不是什么全新的消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we feel like the adversary landscape is getting quite a bit better quite quickly.
zh: 但我们感觉对手的态势正在相当快地变强。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it went from something that we already had a ton of attention on to something we were spending even more attention on.
zh: 所以它从一件我们本来就已经高度关注的事，变成了一件我们投入更多关注的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it does feel like, say over the next five years, you're going to see more breaches than you did over the past five years.
zh: 而且确实感觉，比如说在未来五年，你会看到比过去五年更多的安全泄露事件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dark.
zh: 黑暗。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is true.
zh: 这是事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, there's no two ways about it.
zh: 就是说，这没什么好争论的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because, again, in theory, there should be some equilibrium between offense and defense.
zh: 因为，同样，理论上，攻防之间应该存在某种均衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's this very, like, assume a spherical cow theory.
zh: 但那是一种非常……「假设一头球形奶牛」式的理论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in practice, there are lots of organizations out there that are going to be too slow in how they adopt the latest capabilities.
zh: 而在实践中，有很多组织在采用最新能力方面会过于迟缓。

speaker: Unknown
en: The good news for, like, the startups in the room is, obviously, I think startups are
zh: 对在座的初创公司来说，好消息是，显然，我认为初创公司

speaker: Unknown
en: disproportionately in the good spot because it is easier for them to adopt the latest models with the latest cyber capabilities and they just have smaller, more contained, more homogenous tech stacks versus if you're running some 50-year-old tech stack that has grown through acquisition where you're running on versions of Windows that aren't even supported anymore, that's not a great place to be in from a cyber point of view.
zh: 处于有利位置的比例格外高，因为它们更容易采用具备最新网络攻击能力的最新模型，而且它们的技术栈更小、更可控、更同质化；相比之下，如果你在运营某个通过收购不断扩张、已有五十年历史的技术栈，跑在甚至不再受支持的 Windows 版本上，从网络安全的角度来看，那不是一个好的处境。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've talked about singularity a bunch.
zh: 所以你谈过很多次奇点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a different perspective on it that I think is like a little bit more optimistic than the standard San Francisco doom.
zh: 你对它的看法有所不同，我认为比旧金山式的标准末日论要乐观一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you, I guess, what is your perspective on singularity?
zh: 那么，我猜，你对奇点的看法是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you make this?
zh: 你是怎么得出这个的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you know, we've been,
zh: 是的，你知道，我们一直在,

speaker: Unknown
en: We kind of somewhat, tongue-in-cheek at Stripe, started referring to January 1st as day one of the singularity.
zh: 我们在 Stripe 有点半开玩笑地开始把 1 月 1 日称为奇点的第一天。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so kind of like the Unix epoch is January 1st, 1970.
zh: 就像 Unix 纪元是 1970 年 1 月 1 日一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We decided that the singularity epoch is January 1st, 2026.
zh: 我们决定奇点纪元是 2026 年 1 月 1 日。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's as good a day as any to decide that we are now in the singularity.
zh: 选这么一天来认定我们现在已经身处奇点之中，再合适不过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not a total coincidence that we picked that date in that, if you guys remember, it was the end of
zh: 我们选这个日期也并非完全巧合，因为如果你们还记得的话，那正是

speaker: Unknown
en: Last year that I feel like for many of us it was the holy crap moment when it came to coding models and how they're getting so good.
zh: 去年的年末，我感觉对我们很多人来说，那是看到编程模型变得如此之好时的「天哪」时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in particular, the thing that all the AI folks talk about is this idea of recursive self-improvement where the AI uses the AI to make itself better.
zh: 尤其是，所有 AI 圈的人都在谈的就是这个递归自我提升的概念，也就是用 AI 来让 AI 自身变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I think sometimes it...
zh: 再说，我觉得有时候这……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bit challenging because people refer to the AI as kind of this monolithic thing, but we're clearly in a world where AI capabilities are helping with the rate of improvement in AI.
zh: 有点棘手，因为人们把 AI 说成是某种单一的整体，但我们显然处于一个 AI 能力正在帮助提升 AI 改进速度的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, just look at all the math announcements that we had this week and last week.
zh: 我是说，只要看看这周和上周所有关于数学的发布就够了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in math wars now.
zh: 我们现在处于数学大战之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just not something that was on my bingo card for 2026 that we have math wars, but, you know, rival math factions.
zh: 这完全不是我 2026 年宾果卡上会有的东西——我们竟然有数学大战，还有对立的数学派系。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we have.
zh: 但确实有了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of the same thing applies to the model development where the labs are using AI capabilities to go faster.
zh: 同样的事情也适用于模型开发，各个实验室正在利用 AI 能力来加快速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anyway, it feels like 2026 is this year where we're really feeling the effects of that recursive self-improvement.
zh: 所以总之，感觉 2026 年是我们真正感受到这种递归自我提升影响的年份。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're pretty optimistic at Stripe.
zh: 我觉得我们在 Stripe 是相当乐观的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We see the early economic indicators from this, where as a result of intelligence on tap getting much cheaper, new firm creation is way up.
zh: 我们看到了由此带来的早期经济指标：由于「随取随用的智能」变得便宜得多，新公司的创建数量大幅上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing the highest rates of new firm creation that we've seen in recent memory on Stripe right now, because when you have all these tools, it's easier to start a company, it's easier to actually make it successful.
zh: 我们目前在 Stripe 上看到的新公司创建率是近期记忆中最高的，因为当你拥有所有这些工具时，创办一家公司变得更容易，让它真正成功也变得更容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this technology has lots to be optimistic about.
zh: 我认为这项技术有很多值得乐观的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we don't see the singularity in any kind of a pessimistic or kind of worried manner.
zh: 所以我们并不以任何悲观或担忧的方式看待奇点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just like we are in this moment of AI takeoff right now, and you should enjoy it.
zh: 只是我们正处于 AI 起飞的这一刻，你应该享受它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's kind of hard to deny that it's happening.
zh: 而且很难否认它正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Should we be scared, or is that just a marketing tactic?
zh: 我们应该感到害怕吗，还是那只是一种营销手段？

speaker: Unknown
en: In a business context, firstly, I think you should be paying attention.
zh: 在商业语境下，首先，我认为你应该保持关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, the thing that we tell businesses, you know, that we're working with at Stripe is, you know, when we're talking about the cyber stuff, all the cyber stuff is real.
zh: 就是说，我们告诉在 Stripe 合作的那些企业的是，你看，当我们谈论网络安全这些事时，所有这些网络安全的事都是真实存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, just as we're talking about the agent of commerce stuff earlier, the entire landscape is shifting.
zh: 再说一次,就像我们之前谈到的 commerce 智能体相关的东西,整个格局都在发生变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you another example.
zh: 我再给你举一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spent
zh: 我们花了

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, again, the entirety of Stripe up to this point, building for developers and using APIs as a selling point.
zh: 你知道,再说一次,Stripe 到目前为止的全部精力,都是在为开发者构建产品,并把 API 作为卖点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like making the developer experience easy was what we focused on, what we spent a huge amount of internal effort on at Stripe.
zh: 比如让开发者体验变得容易,是我们在 Stripe 内部投入了大量精力去关注的重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this would be like minute details of the API documentation or how we make upgrades easy for a developer who's migrating from, you know, one version of the API to the other.
zh: 这可以小到 API 文档里的细节,或者我们如何让开发者从一个版本的 API 迁移到另一个版本时升级变得容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Overnight, relatively overnight, no one actually really integrates the Stripe API by hand anymore.
zh: 几乎是一夜之间,实际上已经没有人再手工集成 Stripe API 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They send their coding agent to do it.
zh: 他们把编码智能体派去干这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a related skill, but it's actually a pretty different skill because the developer ergonomics are different from the AI ergonomics.
zh: 这是一项相关的技能,但实际上是相当不同的技能,因为开发者的人体工学和 AI 的人体工学是不一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so many of the things that we spend time on to make things nice for developers actually don't really matter to the AIs.
zh: 我们花了很多时间做的许多让开发者觉得方便的事情,实际上对 AI 来说并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what matters is a fairly different set of things.
zh: 而重要的是一套相当不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very easy for them to
zh: 对 AI 来说,它们很容易

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, integrate the wrong version of the API or something like this.
zh: 集成错误版本的 API,或者出类似的错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we are having to kind of totally change what we're good at internally at Stripe.
zh: 所以我们不得不彻底改变 Stripe 内部所擅长的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's probably true for all the industries people are working in here, where just everyone's chessboard just got a little bit of a jiggle and some of the pieces got knocked and, you know, the position moved around.
zh: 我想这对在座的各位所在的行业可能都是成立的,每个人的棋盘都稍微被晃了一下,有些棋子被碰倒了,你知道,位置发生了变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now you're working with this new chess position.
zh: 所以现在你是在一个新的棋局里工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everyone needs to...
zh: 我认为每个人都需要……

speaker: Unknown
en: Pay advantage to that.
zh: 注意到这个优势。

en: If people are visiting from out of town, you've got to get, like, outside of SOMA.

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you're, like, coming to this conference and you're staying in Union Square or whatever, the key thing is you've got to get outside of this one block where it is, especially while Dreamforce is on.
zh: 所以如果你是来参加这个大会、住在联合广场或什么的，关键就是你要走出这一个个街区，尤其是在 Dreamforce 举办期间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, good God.
zh: 我的意思是，天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that is my main encouragement, too.
zh: 所以这也是我的主要鼓励。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also will help with avoiding the AI psychosis.
zh: 这也有助于避免 AI psychosis。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it does surprise me, because I visit here quite often, I don't live here, that people come here as tourists.
zh: 我的意思是，这确实让我惊讶，因为我经常来这儿，但我不住在这里，居然有人来这里旅游。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's beautiful.
zh: 但这里很美。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course I do.
zh: 我当然会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know.
zh: 我知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'm just used to coming here, and it's like an office park.
zh: 但我只是习惯了来这儿，这里就像一个办公园区。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: But people come here because of culture.
zh: 但人们来这里是因为文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know if I'd say culture, but.
zh: 我不确定我会说是因为文化,不过。

speaker: Unknown
en: History.
zh: 历史。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nature.
zh: 自然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what do you think, maybe this is a little bit more of a tricky question, but what do you think are the main or one of the questions that isn't being asked right now in this era, AI, agents, computer, that we should be asking?
zh: 那么你觉得——也许这个问题有点难——你认为在这个 AI、智能体、计算机的时代,有哪些主要的、或者其中一个现在没人问、但我们本应该问的问题是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, one, like I said, is, I think this is being asked, but I think it's going to become a much louder and more pointed question, is, for example, many sites do bot detection and bot prevention, and that is a reasonable thing to do, or, like, it's understandable how they got there, but, like, it's increasingly all bots.
zh: 嗯,首先,就像我说的,我认为这个问题已经有人在问了,但我认为它会成为一个越来越响亮、越来越尖锐的问题,比如,很多网站会做机器人检测和机器人防护,这样做是合理的,或者说,可以理解他们为什么会走到这一步,但,如今几乎全都是机器人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what is the new equivalent of
zh: 那么,新的等价物是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, bot detection for the world we are going to where there is the good bots and then there are the bad bots and you need to be able to screen between them.
zh: 你知道,在我们正在走向的那个世界里,机器人检测应该是什么样的——那里有好机器人,也有坏机器人,你需要能够在两者之间进行甄别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, again, I think we are just at this really interesting moment happening now where, again, as I see it, you really should play with one of, you know, Instinct or GrokBot or
zh: 所以,再说一次,我认为我们现在正处在这个非常有趣的时刻,再次强调,在我看来,你真的应该去玩一玩其中一个,你知道,Instinct 或者 GrokBot,或者

speaker: Unknown
en: Muse from Meta or any of these kind of AI assistant tools because they're a very powerful sense of what is coming and that new modality for how AI products will work.
zh: Meta 的 Muse,或者任何这类 AI 助手工具,因为它们非常有力地预示了即将到来的东西,以及 AI 产品将如何运作的那种新模态。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, I think they ask a lot of questions about what the new equilibrium will be, and I think we just don't know that.
zh: 但再说一次,我认为它们引出了很多关于新均衡将会是什么样的问题,而我们只是不知道答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we close out, I have one last question, but over 17 years as a founder, what have been your biggest lessons?
zh: 在收尾之际,我还有最后一个问题,在 17 年的创始人生涯中,你学到的最大的经验教训是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, I think if you're really looking to condense the Stripe story or Stripe experience, one, I'd say there's no shortcuts.
zh: 你看,我想如果你真的想把 Stripe 的故事或 Stripe 的经历浓缩一下,第一,我要说没有捷径。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stripe never had a South by Southwest breakout moment.
zh: Stripe 从来没有过在 South by Southwest 上爆红的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were times when it would be flicking the growth dial and saying, is this thing on?
zh: 有时候就像拨动增长的旋钮,然后问,这东西开着吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And just it was growing.
zh: 然后它就在增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every year has been a bigger year than the prior year.
zh: 每一年都比前一年规模更大。

speaker: Unknown
en: It turns out you just do that enough years.
zh: 事实证明,你只要这样坚持足够多的年头。

speaker: Unknown
en: One after another, and you eventually get to $1.9 trillion.
zh: 一年接着一年,你最终就能达到 1.9 万亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it never felt like, oh, my God, this thing is really working.
zh: 但从来没有那种感觉,天哪,这东西真的在起作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just felt like, oh, yeah, I mean, growth is down a bit from last year, but in absolute terms, it's bigger.
zh: 只是感觉,哦,是的,我的意思是,增长比去年降了一点,但绝对值上更大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you eventually get there.
zh: 然后你最终就到达了那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a lot of years of that.
zh: 而且这样的年份有很多很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And similarly, we'd invest everything
zh: 同样地,我们会投入一切

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is obviously kind of definitionally true.
zh: 我是说,这显然在定义上就是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every new product you start is kind of immaterial and a toy to begin with.
zh: 你启动的每一个新产品,一开始都是无足轻重的,像个玩具。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we rarely started products that felt like the future of the company at the time.
zh: 但我们很少启动那些在当时就让人觉得是公司未来的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just started a neat thing that we thought delivered value for customers.
zh: 我们只是启动了一个我们觉得能为客户创造价值的不错的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think...
zh: 但这真是一个坚持不懈的故事,因为有很多时期,NVIDIA 远没有今天这么火热。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a real element of Stripe that is just stick-with-edness where we didn't quit and we didn't get acquired and we just stayed plugging away at it.
zh: Stripe 有一个很关键的特质,就是坚持不懈,我们没有放弃,没有被收购,我们就这么一直埋头干下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's underrated in a lot of tech stories.
zh: 我认为这在很多科技故事里被低估了。

speaker: Unknown
en: NVIDIA is the largest company in the world.
zh: NVIDIA 是世界上最大的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they've just been making GPUs since the 1990s.
zh: 而他们从上世纪 90 年代就一直在制造 GPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they made better GPUs.
zh: 他们制造了更好的 GPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, I think they thought of improvements like, oh, we should have CUDA.
zh: 再说一次,我想他们也想到了像这样的改进,哦,我们应该做 CUDA。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they thought of these improvements to have.
zh: 他们想到了这些可以做的改进。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's a real story of stick-with-edness because there were many periods when NVIDIA was much less hot than it is today.
zh: 但这确实是一个关于坚持不懈的真实故事，因为有很多时期，NVIDIA 都远不如今天这么火热。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we always tried to play the long-term game, you know, infinite game with people where you want to do right by your partners and you want to be seen as good to work with.
zh: 我认为我们一直试图打长期的游戏,你知道,和人们玩无限游戏,你想善待你的合作伙伴,你想被视为一个很好共事的对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think reputation matters a lot.
zh: 我认为声誉非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we care about Stripe having a reputation for being a good company to work with.
zh: 你知道,我们在乎 Stripe 拥有一个"很好共事的公司"的声誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think just treating being a good counterparty seriously or something is
zh: 所以我认为,认真地对待做一个好的交易对手这件事,或者类似的,

speaker: Unknown
en: is something that really matters.
zh: 是真正重要的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the last one is...
zh: 然后最后一个是……

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk about this at Stripe.
zh: 我们在 Stripe 内部会讨论这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a set of operating principles in terms of how we work.
zh: 我们有一套关于如何工作的运营原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lots of businesses have them.
zh: 很多企业都有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our first one is just users first.
zh: 我们的第一条就是用户优先。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we always try to start with, what does the customer actually want, and work backwards from that, especially when it comes to product development.
zh: 我们总是试着从「客户到底想要什么」出发,再从那里倒推,尤其是在产品开发方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's very easy for companies to go adrift and start getting into, you know what market we should get into, or a great new revenue pool would be X, or really get into this
zh: 而且我觉得公司很容易迷失方向,开始陷入「我们应该进入什么市场」,或者「下一个很好的营收池会是 X」,或者真的陷入这种——

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an internal, company-oriented way of thinking.
zh: 这是一种内部的、以公司为导向的思维方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's fine to do, and people can like their spreadsheets or anything like that.
zh: 那么做也没问题,人们可以喜欢他们的表格之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, John Carlson, thank you so much, and thank you to Paul and everyone at BrowserBase and all of you for coming today.
zh: 好了,John Carlson,非常感谢你,也感谢 Paul 以及 BrowserBase 的所有人,还有今天到场的各位。
